I farm all 16.1 mu in the usual wheat-maize rotation, so I will put the full area into winter wheat first and then summer maize on the same land after wheat harvest. I am 63 and farming mostly by experience, so I will keep the plan steady and practical instead of trying anything risky. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on that to protect yield, especially at the key stages for wheat and maize. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate but solid fertilizer, and about three irrigations because wheat here responds well when water is secure. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I care most about stable output, and I will keep fertilizer a little heavier on nitrogen since maize needs it. I will keep pesticide use limited but not skip it, because if weeds, insects, or disease get ahead of me, it costs more in yield than the spray costs me. I will use rotary tillage where it fits the rotation and my labor, because it is easier for me to manage on my own and works fine on this farm.
